Name: Project FENRIR
Description:
FENRIR (Free fall Experiment uNit for Reduced gravity Investigation and Research) is a student-led space project from Luleå University of Technology (LTU) in Kiruna, Sweden. The project aims to create an easy-to-use platform for ejecting scientific payloads from sounding rockets. The Free Fall Unit (FFU) will carry two payloads: an attitude stabilisation system (ATSS) and an experiment in the field of phase change materials (PCM).

FENRIR is a part of the REXUS/BEXUS programme and is set to fly on the RX34 sounding rocket in March 2025. REXUS/BEXUS is a student experiment programme financed by the Swedish National Space Agency and the German Aerospace Centre with support from the European Space Agency - ESA, the Swedish Space Corporation - SSC, ZARM and more.

Name: MARA.REXUS
Description:
MARA is an experiment with the objective of simulating material acquisition of an asteroid and investigating the feasibility of core drilling as a method of material acquisition in a spacelike environment.

This is realised by designing, manufacturing, testing and launching an experimental setup with asteroid simulant, a drilling rig, and sensors to measure and validate the experiment.

MARA is a student led experiment project of Space Campus Kiruna at Luleå University of Technology (LTU). We have been selected to participate in the REXUS/BEXUS programme to place our experiment on a REXUS rocket. Sending the experiment module ~80km from the surface of the Earth and giving us the opportunity to conduct our experiment in a reduced gravity environment. Further simulating the asteroid like environment. The launch of MARA is scheduled for March 2027 from Esrange space center in Kiruna.

Qinematic Space develops an easy‐to‐use, markerless motion capture system for astronaut training, pre‐habilitation, and rehabilitation on Earth.

Name: Mars Society Sweden
Description:
Mars Society Sweden is the official Swedish chapter of the Mars Society.

Mars Society Sweden was founded in 2021 after our chairperson, Dr Magdalena Pfaffl, met with Robert Zubrin and Lucinda Offer at 2019’s European Mars Conference in London.

Our board consists of professionals in engineering and humanities. It is our aim to invite everyone to the table and show that both sciences and humanities have a stake and a role to play in the settlement of Mars.

Our mission is to:

- Further interest in Mars exploration and settlement through outreach and education.

- Be the main point of contact for every Swedish resident with interest in or questions about Mars exploration and settlement.

and

- Inform policy and lobby for Swedish participation in private space enterprise.
